amusement.definition: the feeling of being entertained or amused.
examples: Her stories brought amusement to the group.

arduous.definition: very difficult and needing a lot of effort.
examples: The hike was arduous but rewarding.

ancient.definition: very old; from a long time ago.
examples: Ancient ruins attract many visitors.

aged.definition: having lived for a specified number of years; old.
examples: Aged trees stood tall.
Are you afraid to try new things?

aunt.definition: The sister of one of your parents; a female relative.
examples: My aunt sent me a birthday card.
Aunt Maria is visiting us this weekend.

astute.definition: Having or showing sharp intelligence and good judgement.
examples: An astute investor will diversify holdings for safety.

apricity.definition: A warmth or sunlight in winter that is pleasant or comforting.
examples: We enjoyed apricity on the park bench during the cold day.

angry.definition: Feeling or showing strong displeasure or hostility.
examples: He was angry about the delay in the project.

act.definition: To take action or behave in a specified way.
examples: We must act quickly to fix the problem.

action.definition: The fact or process of doing something to achieve a result.
examples: The plan requires swift action.

active.definition: Engaged in a task or in movement; not passive.
examples: She stays physically active with regular workouts.

activate.definition: To make something start working or effective; to set in motion.
examples: Press the button to activate the device.

altar.definition: A raised place used for offering or presenting religious offerings.
examples: The wedding took place at the altar.
Azure waters stretched to the horizon.

anthropology.definition: The study of humans, past and present, including cultures and societies.
examples: Her major is anthropology.

actor.definition: A person who performs in plays, movies, or on television.
examples: The actor spent months preparing for the role.
She became a famous actor after starring in several hit movies.

awesome.definition: Extremely good or impressive; inspiring awe.
examples: The view from the top of the mountain was awesome.
You did an awesome job on the presentation.

amice.definition: a stiff cloth or garment part worn by clergy, especially in church services
examples: The amice is part of the church clothing in the story.

alb.definition: a long white robe worn in Christian religious services
examples: The priest wore an alb for the service.

amble.definition: to walk slowly without a clear destination
examples: They amble down the street every morning.
I am just ambling along, not rushing.

altruistic.definition: showing concern for other people and wanting to help them
examples: She is altruistic and always volunteers.
They took an altruistic approach to the problem.

anecdote.definition: a short story about a real event, usually told to share information or entertain
examples: She told an anecdote about her first job.
An anecdote can make a lesson easier to remember.

arcane.definition: understood by only a few people, or known for being mysterious
examples: The rules seem arcane to new players.
Some of the chemistry is arcane to me.

adroit.definition: skilled and quick in how you handle situations or people
examples: She is adroit at negotiating.
He made adroit moves during the game.

artist.definition: a person who creates art such as paintings, drawings, or sculptures
examples: She is an artist who paints landscapes.
The artist will display new work next month.
The music was audible even outside.
I could not make out the words, but the sound was audible.

audience.definition: a group of people who watch a performance or listen to a talk
examples: The audience applauded at the end.
We need to impress the audience quickly.
Auditory tests measure how well you hear.
The doctor gave auditory instructions.

auditor.definition: a person or company that checks and verifies financial records
examples: An auditor reviewed the company’s accounts.
The auditor found a mistake.
The streetlight glowed amber.
She wore an amber scarf.

ascribe.definition: to believe that something is caused by a particular thing or person
examples: They ascribed the delay to traffic.
We ascribed her success to hard work.

anxious.definition: worried or nervous about something that might happen
examples: I am anxious about the test.
She felt anxious waiting for the call.

aquatic.definition: related to water or living in or near water
examples: Aquatic animals live in rivers and lakes.
They built an aquatic habitat for the fish.

aquifer.definition: an underground layer of rock or sand that holds water
examples: The city gets water from an aquifer.
Overuse can reduce the aquifer.

aquarium.definition: a tank of water with glass sides where people keep fish and other sea animals
examples: We visited an aquarium downtown.
Our aquarium has tropical fish.

aqueous.definition: made of water or mixed with water
examples: The solution is aqueous.
Aqueous chemicals are easier to handle.

air.definition: the gas that surrounds the Earth and we breathe
examples: The air feels cold today.
Please open the window for some fresh air.

apple.definition: a round fruit with skin that is usually red, green, or yellow
examples: I ate an apple.
She bought a bag of apples.

axe.definition: a tool with a heavy metal head used for cutting wood
examples: He used an axe to split the log.
Be careful with the axe.

axe.definition: to cut or remove something quickly and forcefully
examples: They decided to axe the project.
The company axed several jobs.

atonement.definition: Something done to make up for a wrongdoing and repair a relationship
examples: He tried to offer atonement after he hurt her feelings.
They held a ceremony for atonement.

architect.definition: A person who designs buildings and oversees their construction
examples: The architect designed the new school building.
She worked with an architect to plan the renovation.

annoyed.definition: Slightly angry or upset because of something unpleasant
examples: She was annoyed that the meeting started late.
I’m annoyed about the delay in the delivery.

anesthetist.definition: A doctor or specialist who gives anesthesia and manages a patient’s pain during surgery
examples: The anesthetist checked her medical history before surgery.
An anesthetist monitored her throughout the operation.

audit.definition: An official check of financial records, usually to confirm accuracy and compliance
examples: The company hired an external audit firm.
The audit found a few accounting errors.

audit.definition: To officially check financial records to confirm accuracy and compliance
examples: They will audit the accounts next month.
The auditors audit the company’s financial statements every year.

auditable.definition: Possible to audit, meaning records can be checked and verified
examples: The system stores data in an auditable format.
Our logs are auditable, so they can be reviewed later.

auditing.definition: The activity of performing an audit to check financial records or processes
examples: Auditing helps ensure accurate reporting.
Auditing will begin after the financial year ends.

allusion.definition: A brief and indirect reference to a person, event, or idea
examples: The movie includes an allusion to a classic novel.
Her joke was an allusion to last year’s incident.

allegory.definition: A story or message that has a hidden meaning, often teaching a moral or idea
examples: The book is an allegory about power and responsibility.
Her speech was an allegory for the situation at work.
The view from the balcony was very alluring.
They found the job offer alluring at first.

apprehensive.definition: Worried or nervous about something that might happen
examples: She felt apprehensive before the interview.
He was apprehensive about traveling alone at night.

apothecary.definition: A person or small shop that sells medicines and makes herbal or medicinal preparations
examples: In the story, the apothecary prepared herbal remedies.
The apothecary sold tinctures and tablets.

advocate.definition: A person who speaks in support of an idea, cause, or person
examples: She is a strong advocate for education reform.
The advocate spoke on behalf of the victims.

advocate.definition: To publicly support a plan, idea, or cause
examples: He advocates stricter safety rules.
They advocate for equal opportunities.

arbiter.definition: A person or group that decides disputes in a fair way
examples: The arbiter made a final ruling.
They appointed an arbiter to resolve the conflict.

airy.definition: Light, not heavy; also, open and not crowded
examples: The room felt airy because the windows were large.
She wore an airy dress.

acerbic.definition: Sharp, sarcastic, and critical in tone
examples: He gave an acerbic reply to the question.
Her acerbic humor made some people uncomfortable.

annotate.definition: To add notes or comments to a text to explain or highlight information
examples: She annotated the article with key definitions.
They annotated the map to show important locations.

abrasion.definition: A scrape or injury to the skin caused by rubbing
examples: He cleaned the abrasion and covered it with a bandage.
The bicycle accident caused a painful abrasion on her knee.

abstain.definition: To choose not to do something, especially a harmful activity or to avoid voting
examples: He abstained from alcohol during the program.
Many members abstained when the vote was taken.

avalanche.definition: A large amount of snow, ice, and rock that falls down a mountain slope
examples: An avalanche buried the road after midnight.
Rescuers searched for survivors after the avalanche.

affidavit.definition: A written statement of facts sworn to be true, signed in front of an authorized person
examples: The court accepted the affidavit as evidence.
He provided an affidavit to support his claim.

apprehension.definition: An anxious feeling that something unpleasant might happen
examples: He tried to hide his apprehension before the exam.
Apprehension grew as the deadline approached.

anesthesia.definition: A medicine or treatment used to prevent pain during medical procedures, often by making a patient unconscious or numb
examples: Anesthesia kept her from feeling pain during surgery.
The anesthesiologist planned the anesthesia carefully.

abrupt.definition: Sudden and unexpected; happening with little warning
examples: There was an abrupt stop in the traffic.
He gave an abrupt answer and left.
